correctness.rationale: The normalized Beta moments give \(c_j=( eta)_j/j!\) and the kernel series. DFT orthogonality proves the exact conditional-residue formula. The expectation/variance derivatives establish global uniqueness for \(m\le N\). Uniform residue-grid Riemann sums establish the sublinear constant; dominated-convergence Fourier-sector sums plus strictly negative variance establish the macroscopic limit and uniqueness. AM–GM and a uniformly geometric positive tail yield \(1-M\sim2\sqrt{c_{N-m}c_{N+m}}/c_N\) when \(m/N	o1^-\). The standalone checker reproduced Gram inverses independently and passed 630 finite assertions; finite tests are not used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The fixed target and regular-polygon kernel dictionary are canonical in rotationally symmetric analytic sampling, so the optimized captured energy measures concrete aliasing loss rather than an arbitrary numerical slice. A single theorem determines the exact finite problem, the optimal sublinear coefficient, the density-dependent nontrivial continuum obstruction and a sharp near-critical square-root recovery law for every standard weighted Bergman exponent. These facts make a reproducible benchmark for structured sparse kernel approximation without claiming unconstrained optimality.
